Gift.name: EXPOSE
Gift.tagline: Addressing the elephant in the room: seeing the cracks others miss or are afraid to name.
Gift.quiz_scenario: A community app's sign-up quietly fails on older phones, and nobody on the team has noticed yet. Which role steps up first?

Gift.name: CHALLENGE
Gift.tagline: Questioning what isn't working, even when it makes the room uncomfortable.
Gift.quiz_scenario: A team keeps missing deadlines and everyone shrugs: “that's just how it is.” Which role questions the process?

Gift.name: ADVOCATE
Gift.tagline: Speaking up for the group when others feel it but won't say it.
Gift.quiz_scenario: Employees keep raising the same concern privately but never in meetings. Which role makes sure it gets heard and handled fairly?

Gift.name: EMPOWER
Gift.tagline: Helping others find the courage to use their own voice.
Gift.quiz_scenario: A new hire has strong ideas but never speaks first in meetings. Which role helps her find the courage to use her voice?

Gift.name: SUPPORT
Gift.tagline: Standing with people through the change so they're not left alone in it.
Gift.quiz_scenario: A family is navigating a hard transition and needs someone to walk alongside them while connecting them to resources. Which role fits?

Job.title: QA Analyst
Job.description: Finds what's broken before others experience it.

Job.title: Community Researcher
Job.description: Uncovers issues affecting communities and brings them into the open.

Job.title: Process Improvement Consultant
Job.description: Challenges how work gets done and helps teams find better ways.

Job.title: Auditor
Job.description: Challenges whether people and systems are held accountable.

Job.title: HR Specialist (Employee Relations)
Job.description: The person employees bring concerns to, so their voice is heard and handled fairly.

Job.title: Customer Success Manager
Job.description: Represents the customer's voice inside a company.

Job.title: Learning & Development Specialist
Job.description: Designs and leads training that helps employees build skills and confidence.

Job.title: Career Coach
Job.description: Helps people find their strengths, speak up for what they want, and go after it.

Job.title: Project Manager
Job.description: Keeps the team moving and supported from start to finish.

Job.title: Social Worker
Job.description: Walks alongside people through hard situations and connects them to the resources they need.

Branch.label: Document it first
Branch.title: Show your work
Branch.text: Before you said a word out loud, you wrote down every step — where it broke, who it cost, what it cost them. Evidence turns a complaint into a case someone has to answer.

Branch.label: Demo the failure
Branch.title: Let them watch it break
Branch.text: You walked someone through the broken flow and let it fail in front of them. Nothing argues like the thing itself failing, live, in the room.

Branch.label: Ask in the room
Branch.title: Say it out loud
Branch.text: You stopped the meeting and asked the question everyone was avoiding. It got quiet. Then someone answered honestly, and the plan changed.

Branch.label: Ask in writing
Branch.title: Put it in the doc
Branch.text: You left the question in the shared doc, where it sat next to the plan and couldn't be talked around. By morning three people had replied with the same concern.

Branch.label: Bring their words
Branch.title: Carry their voice in
Branch.text: You brought the actual quotes — what the user said, not your summary of it. The room stopped designing for an idea of a person and started designing for a person.

Branch.label: Bring their case
Branch.title: Build the business case
Branch.text: You translated a person's frustration into hours lost and money wasted. The spreadsheet was never the point, but it's what got the decision made.

Branch.label: Teach one person
Branch.title: Make one expert
Branch.text: You sat with one teammate until they could do it without you — then you got out of the way. One person now does it faster than you ever did.

Branch.label: Teach the room
Branch.title: Write the guide
Branch.text: You wrote the steps down so nobody needs you standing behind them. The guide outlived the meeting, the team, and the launch.

Branch.label: Stay through the launch
Branch.title: Stay for the hard part
Branch.text: You stayed when it broke at 2am and the room got quiet. Support isn't the credit-taking part; it's the part where you're still there.

Branch.label: Follow up after
Branch.title: Come back a week later
Branch.text: You came back a week later to ask whether it was actually better. Nobody asked you to. That's the difference between shipping and helping.

Action.text: Complete a course on root cause analysis (5 Whys, fishbone diagrams) on LinkedIn Learning or Coursera.
Action.explain: Root cause analysis means finding the real reason something broke, not just the first thing you notice.

Action.text: Study for and earn the ISTQB Foundation Level software testing certification.
Action.explain: This is a well-known certification for software testers. It proves I know how to find bugs the right way.

Action.text: Keep a Blind Spot journal weekly for 30 days, then review it for patterns.
Action.explain: Every week I write down things I might be missing. After a month, I look back for patterns.

Action.text: Interview or shadow a QA analyst or community researcher.
Action.explain: Shadowing means following someone at work for a day to see what the job is really like.

Action.text: Lead a team retrospective after each project milestone.
Action.explain: A retro is a team talk after a project: what went well, what didn't, and what to fix next time.

Action.text: Complete Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt training.
Action.explain: A beginner training on making work run smoother, with fewer mistakes and less waste.

Action.text: Read Crucial Conversations and practice one technique in a team meeting.
Action.explain: A book about staying calm and clear in hard talks, when people disagree and the stakes are high.

Action.text: Map one team process and present one improvement within 30 days.
Action.explain: I draw out how my team does a task, step by step, then suggest one way to make it better.

Action.text: Attend an intro webinar from the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA).
Action.explain: The IIA is the main group for auditors. Their intro webinar shows how audits keep people and systems accountable.

Action.text: Ask a mentor once a month for feedback on how a challenge I raised landed.
Action.explain: Once a month, I ask a mentor how my pushback came across, so I can challenge in a way people can hear.

Action.text: Join Toastmasters to strengthen public speaking.
Action.explain: A club where people practice public speaking and get friendly feedback.

Action.text: Study for the aPHR (Associate Professional in Human Resources) certification from HRCI.
Action.explain: A beginner HR certification. It shows I know how to support employees fairly.

Action.text: Complete a free customer service or customer success course on HubSpot Academy.
Action.explain: A free online course about helping customers succeed and feel heard.

Action.text: Create an anonymous feedback form so my team or cohort can share concerns safely.
Action.explain: A form where people can share concerns without giving their name, so it feels safe to speak up.

Action.text: Host a monthly listening session and share the themes with mentors or leadership.
Action.explain: A monthly meeting where I mostly listen, then share the main themes with leaders.

Action.text: Complete an intro coaching course on LinkedIn Learning or Coursera.
Action.explain: A short course on helping people find their own answers, instead of handing them mine.

Action.text: Read Dare to Lead by Brené Brown and apply one idea with my team.
Action.explain: A book by Brené Brown about brave, honest leadership. I'll try one idea from it with my team.

Action.text: Facilitate one workshop or skill-share for my cohort within 60 days.
Action.explain: I'll teach my cohort something I'm good at, so others can grow too.

Action.text: Volunteer as a mentor with a local youth or workforce program for 3 months.
Action.explain: For 3 months, I'll mentor young people or adults who are building their careers.

Action.text: Once a week for 30 days, invite a quieter teammate to share their idea first before I speak.
Action.explain: Once a week, I'll ask a quieter teammate to share their idea first, before I speak.

Action.text: Get certified in Mental Health First Aid.
Action.explain: A training that teaches how to notice when someone is struggling and help them get support.

Action.text: Complete an intro change management course on LinkedIn Learning or Coursera and learn the ADKAR model.
Action.explain: ADKAR is a simple way to help people through change: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement.

Action.text: Read Radical Candor by Kim Scott.
Action.explain: A book about caring about people while still being honest with them.

Action.text: Hold one-on-one check-ins with each teammate every two weeks during a project.
Action.explain: Every two weeks, I'll meet with each teammate one-on-one to see how they're really doing.

Action.text: Follow up within 48 hours with the people affected after any hard conversation or change I lead.
Action.explain: After a hard talk or a big change, I'll check in with the people affected within two days.
